quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following helps direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning on some highways?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows show which lanes to use for different purposes, like going straight or turning.

questions.question: When can you text while driving?

options.text: At any time if you are under 18.
At any time if you are 18 or older.
If you can text without looking at your phone.

questions.explanation: You cannot text while driving except in emergencies. Taking your eyes off the road, even for a moment, increases the chance of a crash.

questions.question: If you drive in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive at no more than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when you cannot see more than 500 feet ahead. Do not use high beams in fog because the light will reflect back and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can hurt your ability to drive. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal to the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another car passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and slow down so the other vehicle can pass easily and get back into the right lane.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed in both directions.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic is moving toward you on the other side. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass, from either direction.

questions.question: It starts to rain while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: When rain makes it hard to see, drive slower. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If the rain is very heavy, pull over and stop until it clears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn at this intersection.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers keeping a four-second distance behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always drive within the speed limit and go slower when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and go with care.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "be careful." When you see this light, slow down, look, and proceed with care.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.

questions.explanation: Quick stops waste fuel because you must accelerate again to reach traffic speed. Drivers who look ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a curve or hill because another vehicle is unlikely to be coming.
By driving on the road shoulder.
If there is a solid yellow line on your side and the passing lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on curves or hills because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Do not drive on the shoulder to pass. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: Why should you be alert to motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They hide easily in blind spots. It is hard to judge their speed and distance. Always watch carefully for motorcycles.

questions.question: When you are in traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before entering the tracks, check that you have enough space to cross without stopping. Never pass another vehicle at or near railroad tracks. Always look for trains before crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and low beam headlights so other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Signal when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn or emergency signals when needed to warn others.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through.
Turn right or left because the road is blocked ahead.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then proceed when traffic allows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then proceed when traffic allows.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians in the intersection, and any other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol affect your driving ability in the same way. Being awake for 18 hours impairs your driving as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours straight impairs your driving as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Blow your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Blow your horn, steer left, and brake.
Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, blow your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: If another vehicle is coming at you head-on in your lane, honk your horn first to get their attention. If they don't move, steer to the right to escape. Swerving left is dangerous because the other driver might correct at the last second and still hit you. If a crash seems unavoidable, brake firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle defect that may affect safe operation. You should:

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you have enough money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that may affect safe operation must be fixed as soon as possible. Fix it before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is not true?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels before winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are best to use in winter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or similar hazardous conditions. Winter is the most difficult driving season and requires extra care. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly in winter. Snow tires improve grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.
